af9.photolithography_line.tooltip.0: §7Prints §fchip wafers§7 through a §freticle§7 (not consumed), one mode per substrate:
af9.photolithography_line.tooltip.2: §e65nm§7 Naquadria, §e50nm§7 Neutronium, §e20nm§7 Transmuted Nt, §e7nm§7 Strange Matter.
af9.photolithography_line.tooltip.3: §7A substrate prints its own chips and all lower ones as GT's wafers, §fmore per print§7 the higher it is.
af9.photolithography_line.tooltip.5: §bVacuum§7: starts at §f0§7 when formed and pumps to §f100§7 in §f10s per version§7 (V1 10s ... V8 80s).
af9.photolithography_line.tooltip.6: §7It holds while the pumps have power; without power it vents to 0 in §c60s§7. Every print can §cbreak§7:
af9.photolithography_line.tooltip.7: §7the finer the node and the dirtier the vacuum, the likelier (§f2%%§7 at 350nm ... §f25%%§7 at 7nm, §c+50%%§7 dirty).
af9.photolithography_line.tooltip.8: §6Versions 1-8§7, like the Assembly Line: one more lens slice each (§f3-10§7), §f10-17§7 blocks long;
af9.photolithography_line.tooltip.9: §7the light source allows up to: §fpurple lamp§7 V1, §fKrF laser§7 V2, §fArF laser§7 V6, §fEUV source§7 V8.
af9.photolithography_line.tooltip.10: §7Per version above a mode: §a0.8x time§7, §a0.75x break chance§7.
af9.photolithography_line.tooltip.11: §7Light: i-line, KrF, ArF, ArF immersion (65nm+), EUV tin plasma (20nm, 7nm).
af9.photolithography_line.tooltip.12: §7Power: up to §f2 Energy Hatches§7; a print needs 4A of the mode's tier (two normal hatches). §aPerfect OC§7.
af9.photolithography_line.tooltip.13: §7Parts are optional, with a maximum: §f2§7 energy, §f8§7 fluid input, §f1§7 maintenance, §f2+2§7 item buses at the controller.
af9.photolithography_line.tooltip.14: §750nm and finer also grow a §fhigh-k gate§7 (Hafnium Tetrachloride).
af9.photolithography_line.tooltip.15: §cWafers contaminate in a player's inventory§7: wear §fRubber Gloves§7 or work in a Cleanroom.
§7Prints §f1 nm§7 chip wafers on §dChromodynium Wafers§7 with an §fX-ray free-electron laser§7.
§cOnly works in orbit§7 (e.g. Ad Astra's Earth Orbit).
§7Power: §f1 Laser Hatch§7 and up to §f3 Energy Hatches§7, §e50A of UHV§7: 100x the energy of a 7 nm print.
§7Resist: one §fMetal-Oxide Dry Resist Cartridge§7 per wafer.
§bVacuum§7 like the line's: §f90s§7 from 0 to 100, vents to 0 in §c60s§7 without power.
§7Breaks §f35%%§7 at a clean vacuum, up to §c85%%§7 dirty.
§7Parts on the inert top deck, all optional with a maximum: §f1§7 laser, §f3§7 energy, §f2§7 coolant, item buses, §f1§7 parallel, §f1§7 maintenance.
§7A §f25x25§7 platform, §f18§7 high: GCYM casings, HSS-S trusses and an HSS-G undulator mast below.
af9.supercooling_cryostat.tooltip.1: §bDense Cooling§7: gas to dense liquid (4:1), the intermediate.
af9.supercooling_cryostat.tooltip.2: §dSupercooling§7: the dense liquid to a supercooled fluid, rated at §b-5000 K§7.
af9.supercooling_cryostat.tooltip.3: §7Hydrogen, argon, xenon and §5endion§7 (from the End's air).
af9.supercooling_cryostat.tooltip.4: §cNeeds 4A of HV§7 (two normal Energy Hatches) to run at all. §aPerfect OC§7.
af9.supercooling_cryostat.tooltip.6: §7Parts are optional, with a maximum: §f2§7 energy, §f2+2§7 fluid hatches, §f1§7 maintenance.
af9.particle_accelerator.tooltip.0: §7A linear accelerator: ion source, eight §fsuperconducting RF cavities§7, a target station.
af9.particle_accelerator.tooltip.1: §aNeutron Irradiation§7: a spallation neutron beam turns §fNeutronium-doped Wafers§7
af9.particle_accelerator.tooltip.3: §6Heavy-Ion Collision§7: lead ions collide, the §fquark-gluon plasma§7 goes into magnetic traps.
af9.particle_accelerator.tooltip.4: §dQuark Synthesis§7: quark-gluon plasma condenses into §fStrange Matter§7, then §fChromodynium§7.
af9.particle_accelerator.tooltip.5: §7Fluids: §fCoolant Hatches only§7 (supercooled hydrogen, argon, xenon, endion).
af9.particle_accelerator.tooltip.6: §7Power: up to §f4§7 Energy Hatches or §f2§7 Laser Hatches, with the recipe's full EU/t.
af9.particle_accelerator.tooltip.7: §7Parts are optional, with a maximum: §f2§7 coolant, §f2+2§7 item buses, §f1§7 maintenance.
af9.particle_accelerator.tooltip.8: §7Beam energy grows with the voltage tier.
af9.coolant_hatch.tooltip.1: §7The only fluid input of the Particle Accelerator and the Orbital Lithography Station.
gtceu.ion_collision.desc: Lead ions collide into quark-gluon plasma
gtceu.quark_synthesis.desc: Quark-gluon plasma condenses into strange matter and chromodynium
af9.smc_large_chemical_reactor.tooltip.0: §7The semiconductor-grade reactor: fab chemistry runs §fonly§7 in SMC machines.
af9.smc_large_chemical_reactor.tooltip.2: §aFilter-casing ceiling: its own clean room (ISO 5). Sterile filters: ISO 3 and 2 parallels.
af9.smc_large_chemical_reactor.tooltip.3: §6One heating coil in the jacket: each coil tier above Cupronickel saves 1/20 of the EU/t (at most half).
af9.smc_large_chemical_reactor.tooltip.4: §dProduct changeover: the first run of a different recipe also takes 1000mB Nitrogen or Argon, 5s more.
af9.smc_large_chemical_reactor.tooltip.5: §7Perfect overclocks, batch mode. Takes one Parallel Hatch and one Laser Hatch.
af9.smc_rectification_column.tooltip.0: §7Packed column for fab gases and solvents, with a cold box for cryogenic work.
af9.smc_rectification_column.tooltip.2: §aEvery tray layer (PTFE Pipe Casing) is a parallel: 1-8 trays.
af9.smc_rectification_column.tooltip.3: §aFilter-casing hood: its own clean room (ISO 5, sterile filters ISO 3).
af9.smc_rectification_column.tooltip.4: §dProduct changeover: 2000mB Nitrogen and 5s more on the first run of a different recipe.
af9.smc_rectification_column.tooltip.5: §7Cuts go to any fluid output hatch. Batch mode, one Parallel Hatch, one Laser Hatch.
af9.smc_membrane_cell_hall.tooltip.0: §7Filter-press stack of membrane cells between titanium electrodes.
af9.smc_membrane_cell_hall.tooltip.2: §aEvery cell (PTFE Pipe Casing between two Titanium Frames) is a parallel: 1-8 cells.
af9.smc_membrane_cell_hall.tooltip.3: §aFilter-casing ceiling: its own clean room (ISO 5, sterile filters ISO 3).
af9.smc_membrane_cell_hall.tooltip.4: §dProduct changeover: the cells are flushed with 1000mB Distilled Water, 5s more.
af9.smc_membrane_cell_hall.tooltip.5: §7Batch mode, one Parallel Hatch, one Laser Hatch.
af9.smc_thermal_processing_furnace.toolt: §7A horizontal tube furnace: calciners, CVD reactors and Czochralski pullers under inert gas.
§6Heats like the Electric Blast Furnace: coil temperature, +100K per energy tier above MV, EBF overclocks.
§dProduct changeover: 1000mB Argon or Nitrogen and 10s more on the first run of a different recipe.
§7No clean room needed. Batch mode, one Parallel Hatch, one Laser Hatch.
af9.smc_chemical_reactor.tooltip.0: §7Fab chemistry: §fSynthesis§7, §fBlending§7, §fWet Processing§7. GT's reactors cannot make it.
af9.smc_chemical_reactor.tooltip.1: §dChangeover: the first run of a different recipe takes 1000mB Nitrogen or Argon, 5s more.
af9.smc_chemical_reactor.tooltip.2: §eFrom HV power on, the recipes need a Cleanroom.
af9.smc_fractionating_still.tooltip.0: §7Batch still: §fFractionation§7 (one column cut per run, circuit = cut) and §fPurification§7.
af9.smc_fractionating_still.tooltip.1: §dChangeover: the first run of a different recipe takes 2000mB Nitrogen, 5s more.
af9.smc_fractionating_still.tooltip.2: §eFrom HV power on, the recipes need a Cleanroom.
af9.smc_electrolytic_cell.tooltip.1: §dChangeover: the cell is flushed with 1000mB Distilled Water, 5s more.
af9.smc_electrolytic_cell.tooltip.2: §eFrom HV power on, the recipes need a Cleanroom.
af9.smc_thermal_furnace.tooltip.1: §dChangeover: the first run of a different recipe takes 1000mB Argon or Nitrogen, 10s more.
af9.smc_thermal_furnace.tooltip.temperat: §6Reaches §f%sK§6, the heat of its tier's coil.
